company: Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage, Inc.
market_holds: There is no usable option chain: the front expiry's ATM legs had no two-sided quotes and total open interest was 62. The usual move is therefore the 7-print history: median |move| 5.04%, 5 of 7 down, the last four in a row down (-12.5% Aug-26 on a Q3 EPS miss, 0.48 vs about 0.52, with a 60bp gross-margin drop and the top of the guide trimmed; -5.0% Nov-25 on the initial FY26 guide). The baseline was sealed at 18:08 UTC. Spot was 26.42 (26.76 in the bars I pulled), -9.5% over 5 days and -18.4% over 20 days, near the post-Q3 low of 26.02. I split the run-in apart with Yahoo bars. NGVC fell -5.4% on 2026-10-29, the day Sprouts fell -22.6% after cutting its outlook. Since then NGVC has drifted with SPY (from 30.12 to about 26.4, -12.3%, against SPY -6.8%), while XLP rose +3.6% and WMK +4.8%. So the run-in holds the Sprouts read-through and the tape, not this company's own guide. Consensus: Q4 EPS about $0.56-0.57 (3 analysts, per FXEmpire/Chartmill/Benzinga snippets), which is the top of the guide-implied range of $0.53-0.57 (FY guide $2.07-2.11 less $1.54 for the nine months). Revenue consensus is $352-360m against $336.1m a year ago. FY26 Street $2.11, the top of the guide. FY27 Street EPS $2.32 (+10%) and revenue $1.44B (+5.5%) per stockanalysis/S&P, from 4 Buy-rated analysts; BofA initiated at Buy with a $35 target on 2026-09-18 and A.G.P. kept Buy at $40 on 2026-09-22, both before Sprouts. Short interest is 7.7-8.5% of float with about 8 days to cover (Chartmill, as of 2026-10-15). The stock trades on comps and traffic, gross margin, and the first FY27 guide, which comes with this print.
view: The deciding line is the first FY27 guide set against a Street of $2.32 that has not been revised. Three things argue that the guide comes in below it. First, the FY26 base flatters: Q3 FY26 operating income of $15.0m included a $2.0m business-interruption insurance gain from the distributor's 2025 cyber incident. Without it, operating income was $13.0m against $15.6m (-17%), and FY26 EPS without the gain is about $2.04-2.05. That makes $2.32 roughly +13% underlying growth. Second, traffic is shrinking: transactions went from +1.0% in Q1 to -1.8% in Q3, and Q3 comps came entirely from basket. Third, the closest peer weakened in this exact calendar quarter. Sprouts' Jul-Sep comps were -0.9% with transactions -3.3%, below the -0.5% to +1.5% guide it gave in late July with July data in hand, and it guided Oct-Dec comps -2% to -4% with price investments in markets that overlap NGVC's (CO, TX, AZ). Management also guides conservatively: the initial FY26 guide had a midpoint of +3.75% growth, the comps guide was cut twice to 1.5-2.0%, and the EPS top was trimmed. A +10% initial midpoint looks unlikely. I put the chance that the guide midpoint lands below $2.32 at roughly 80%. For Q4, the guide needs 2.7-4.7% comps against 1.2% in Q3, on a lap that is 3.2 points easier (4.2% a year ago against 7.4%). A soft quarter at the low end is the likeliest case, with EPS around $0.53-0.55 against $0.56. Revenue consensus at $359m looks too high on my arithmetic (comps near 3% plus about 2 points from new stores gives roughly $350-353m), and NGVC missed its revenue consensus a year ago too ($336m against $351m). So my lean is down. Two things keep me from a call. The price has already de-rated with the sector to 11.4x the stale FY27 number, so some buy-side scepticism is plausibly already in. And Q4 should print an 'acceleration' headline (from 0.5% to 1.2% to about 3%) on the easier lap, with a crowded short in a thin overnight market.
unpriced: The sell-side FY27 number ($2.32, +10% on a base that includes a one-off $0.065 insurance gain) has not been revised since Sprouts' 2026-10-28 cut. The stock's own move ties to the Sprouts read-through and the tape, not to an NGVC guide below Street. Thin coverage and stale estimates are the bias. How much buy-side expectations already sit below that number cannot be shown, so this gap is only partly unpriced.

recommendation.reason: The mechanism is a likely initial FY27 guide below an unrevised $2.32 Street, on an FY26 base flattered by a one-off insurance gain, while traffic falls and Sprouts is cutting prices in overlapping markets. It is real, and this release reveals it at the next open. But the stock has already fallen 18% with the sector and the tape to about 11.4x that stale number. Q4 should show comp acceleration on an easier lap, and short interest at about 8 days to cover makes a less-bad guide a squeeze risk. Confidence of 62 is below the 65 bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An FY27 EPS guide with a midpoint at or above about $2.30 together with a comps guide of 2% or more and positive Q1-to-date transactions (share gain from Sprouts' troubles) would turn this into an up move, likely larger than usual given the short base.

self_critique: The stock is already down 18% in 20 days and near its post-Q3 low at 11.4x a stale number, so the buy side may already expect a guide around $2.15-2.25. If the guide lands there it could be read as clearing the de-rated bar. Q4 laps a 3.2-point easier compare and a cyber-depressed July, so the release may well show comps accelerating to about 3%, plus a DoorDash tailwind. Grocery Outlet's traffic improved in the same quarter, and some of Sprouts' weakness is its own (cyclospora, pricing reset, self-distribution), which NGVC could gain share from. Roughly 8 days to cover in a thin name means a non-disaster print could gap up hard at the open. A year ago the guide beat Street and the stock still fell 5%, which says the reaction runs on comps and traffic tone more than on the EPS gap. That cuts both ways for my mechanism. This case is strong enough that I moved p_up once toward 50 (from 35 to 38).
approach_notes: Three parts of the playbook paid here: P6's instruction to take the run-in apart (the fall is the Sprouts read-through plus the tape, not NGVC news), P4's 'priced is a claim to prove' (FY27 Street unrevised), and rebuilding the line from primary parts, which exposed the insurance gain. The usual gap remains: with no options anchor and no buy-side expectations visible, P7's estimate of the line lands below a stale consensus, but the playbook gives no way to tell how much a sector de-rating already discounts it.
